'''Abdusalam Abubakar''' (born 1989/1990)<ref name="Dublin student wins Young Scientist prize"/> is a [[Somalia|Somali]]-born Irish scientist from [[Dublin]]. He was the winner of the 43rd [[Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition]] in 2007 at the age of seventeen. He went on to be named [[European Union Contest for Young Scientists|EU Young Scientist of the Year]] in September 2007.

==Biography==
Abubakar was born in [[Somalia]] to an Irish father<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR"/> of Somali descent. He is an only child.<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR"/> He moved to Ireland in May 2005,<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR"/> joining [[Synge Street CBS]] in central [[Dublin]].<ref name="Dublin student wins Young Scientist prize"/> He first entered the Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition alongside two fellow students who invited him along and taught him to research and solve properly.<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR"/> They won an award for [[mathematics]] at the event.<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR"/> He was mentored by [[Jim Cooke]].

Abubakar then re-entered the Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition for the 2007 event as a third-year student at Synge Street CBS.<ref name="Dublin student wins Young Scientist prize"/> His project at the exhibition was titled "An Extension of Wiener's Attack on [[RSA (algorithm)|RSA]]".<ref name="Special awards"/> His project was based on the topic of [[cryptography]].<ref name="Dublin student wins Young Scientist prize"/>

Abubakar won the Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition at the [[Royal Dublin Society|RDS]], Dublin, on 12 January 2007.<ref name="Dublin student wins Young Scientist prize">{{cite news | url = http://www.rte.ie/news/2007/0112/scientist.html | title = Dublin student wins Young Scientist prize | date = 12 January 2007 | publisher = [[Raidió Teilifís Éireann]] | accessdate = 15 January 2010 | quote = 17-year-old student ... Abu Salam Abu Bakar}}</ref> He defeated runner-up [[Beara Community School]] in County Cork's Ciara Murphy and her study on hearing loss in teenagers.<ref name="Special awards">{{cite news | url = http://www.independent.ie/national-news/special-awards-59197.html | title = Special awards | date = 13 January 2007 | publisher = [[Irish Independent]] | accessdate = 15 January 2010}}</ref> He admitted afterwards that he had never used a computer before coming to Ireland twenty months earlier.<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR"/>

An interview with Abubakar in ''[[Xclusive Magazine]]'' called him "the hottest name in Ireland right now" and said the achievement was "obviously a landmark in science" after his win.<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR">{{cite news | url = http://www.xclusive.ie/08/abubakar.html | title = ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR | work = [[Xclusive Magazine]] | accessdate = 15 January 2010 | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20070703190049/http://www.xclusive.ie/08/abubakar.html | archivedate = 3 July 2007}}</ref> He appeared on the front cover of that edition of the magazine, under the headline "GENIUS! How Abdusalam Abubakar, a sixteen-year-old Somali, broke a 13-year-old Irish record".<ref name="ABDUSALAM ABUBAKAR"/> Abubakar appeared on ''[[Dustin's Daily News]]'' on 19 January 2007.<ref name="January 19th - Abdusalam Abubakar">{{cite news | url = http://www.rte.ie/tv/theden/ddn/ddn_avlong.html?2170453,240,230 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20080216103241/http://www.rte.ie/tv/theden/ddn/ddn_avlong.html?2170453,240,230 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 16 February 2008 | title = January 19th – Abdusalam Abubakar | date = 12 January 2007 | publisher = [[Dustin's Daily News]] | accessdate = 15 January 2010 | quote = In Turkey Towers there's Young Scientist winner Abdusalam Abubakar. Plus there's more Beak Beak Brother and Niamh reports on more of Ireland's top young scientists.}}</ref>

He went on to represent Ireland at the 19th [[European Union Contest for Young Scientists]] in [[Valencia, Spain|Valencia]], Spain, in September 2007, claiming first prize in the field of [[mathematics]] for Ireland.<ref name="The 19th European Union Contest for Young Scientists">{{cite news | url = http://ec.europa.eu/research/youngscientists/valencia/prize_winners_en.htm | title = The 19th European Union Contest for Young Scientists | publisher = [[European Union Contest for Young Scientists]] | date = 14–19 September 2007 | accessdate = 15 January 2010 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20080521020503/http://ec.europa.eu/research/youngscientists/valencia/prize_winners_en.htm | archivedate = 21 May 2008 | df = dmy-all }}</ref>

Abubakar studied financial mathematics at [[Dublin City University]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Previous Young Scientist winners: where are they now?|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/50yearsyoungscientists/previous-young-scientist-winners-where-are-they-now-254491.html|accessdate=18 June 2016|work=The Irish Examiner|date=9 January 2014}}</ref>
